rules: 723.1. Some cards allow a player to control another player during that player’s next turn. This effect applies to the next turn that the affected player actually takes. The affected player is controlled during the entire turn; the effect doesn’t end until the beginning of the next turn.
723.1a Multiple player-controlling effects that affect the same player overwrite each other. The last one to be created is the one that works.
723.1b If a turn is skipped, any pending player-controlling effects wait until the player who would be affected actually takes a turn.

rules: 302.6. A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol or the untap symbol in its activation cost can’t be activated unless the creature has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began. A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began. This rule is informally called the “summoning sickness” rule.

701.35a Certain spells and abilities can detain a permanent. Until the next turn of the controller of that spell or ability, that permanent can’t attack or block and its activated abilities can’t be activated.
702.10b If a creature has haste, it can attack even if it hasn’t been controlled by its controller continuously since their most recent turn began. (See rule 302.6.)

702.10c If a creature has haste, its controller can activate its activated abilities whose cost includes the tap symbol or the untap symbol even if that creature hasn’t been controlled by that player continuously since their most recent turn began. (See rule 302.6.)

limits: Controlled partial four-player boards, not complete legal-deck games. Native scenarios cover both stack-copy modes; original LKI contracts do not copy a game. Packaged cases use stack copying.
Native attack/block eligibility predicates are observed at fixed main-phase checkpoints. Full declaration policy and strategic AI choices are not certified.

Detain mana-ability admission is checked using Llanowar Elves. A paid newly controlled Prodigal Pyromancer loses Fervor to Naturalize; only the native action-admission result is asserted, not a forced illegal activation.

Detain deadlines use native phase progression without response priority. Player departure, other controllers/targets, untap-symbol costs, arbitrary control histories and other historical consumers remain unverified.
Raw control-age and independent Detain collections are restored without applying new effects or changing ordinary copiable characteristics or physical zone-change copies.

Unmapped callback diagnostics are asserted in fixtures and not yet aggregated into regular CLI reports. Other callbacks, hidden/merged/perpetual state and arbitrary suspended continuations remain open.

Catalog construction proves script availability rather than full gameplay correctness. Seven unavailable entries are nonstarting meld results. Versioned references are not a complete current-rules audit.
